keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 macro nature photo. A thin lime tree twig with a few glossy dark-green citrus leaves. One wide citrus leaf lies almost flat across the middle of the frame, seen from about 45 degrees above, with a clear central vein running from the bottom to the top of the frame. Background: soft out-of-focus green garden. On the upper part of the leaf, just above the center of the frame, sits one single tiny round pale-yellow butterfly egg. The egg is small but clearly visible. The center of the leaf below the egg is empty. Nothing else is on the leaf. Soft diffused daylight, shallow depth of field, sharp focus on the leaf. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the leaf, the twig, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The egg is now an empty pale shell with an open top, in the same spot. One tiny young lime swallowtail caterpillar sits on the leaf right next to the empty shell. It is glossy dark brown with a white band across the middle of its back and small bumps, so it looks like a bird dropping. It is about three times the length of the egg. Only one caterpillar.

Edit this image. Keep the leaf, the empty egg shell, the twig, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. Remove the small brown caterpillar. One large, plump lime swallowtail caterpillar rests along the central vein of the leaf in the center of the frame, below the empty egg shell, head toward the top of the frame. It is smooth bright green with thin pale bands, a dark false eye-spot pattern behind the head, and a brown and white diagonal band near the middle of its body. Its body is about one quarter of the frame height long. Only one caterpillar.

Edit this image. Keep the leaf, the empty egg shell, the twig, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. Replace the caterpillar with one green swallowtail chrysalis in the same spot on the central vein of the leaf. It is attached at its tail end and held by a thin silk girdle around its middle, angled slightly up from the leaf. The chrysalis is angular, with two short points at the head end, smooth leaf-green with faint yellow lines. It is about one fifth of the frame height long. It has no legs and no head. Only one chrysalis.

Edit this image. Keep the leaf, the empty egg shell, the twig, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The chrysalis is now an empty, pale, see-through shell split open at the head end, still attached in the same spot. One newly emerged lime swallowtail butterfly clings to the empty chrysalis with its legs. Its wings are still small, soft and crumpled, hanging down, black with yellow patches. Its body is black and pale yellow. Only one butterfly.

Edit this image. Keep everything exactly the same, including the leaf, the empty egg shell, the empty chrysalis, the twig, background, lighting and camera angle. The butterfly stays in the same spot on the empty chrysalis, but its wings are now fully expanded and spread open flat. The wings are black with many yellow spots and bands, a small red and blue eyespot near the inner edge of each hindwing, and no tails. The wingspan is about two thirds of the frame width. Only one butterfly.
